en: Now, meditation.
As long as the delusion of duality persists, there is neither peace nor supreme bliss.
Therefore, for that purpose, I shall here declare this [teaching] which brings about the realization of the self-nature of all.
Now begins the *Śrī Dattasahasranāmastotra*, beginning with the letter "D" (*dakārādi*).
Oṃ! Dattātreya, full of compassion; Datta, the performer of the duties of a foster-son;
the giver of fearlessness; the giver of fortitude; the one who delights in giving; the destroyer of fear. || 1 ||
The divine one, the slayer of demons, the giver of gifts, the lord of gifts, the sovereign of the givers of gifts;
the dweller in the waters, the bearer of the waters, the one who reclines upon the waters, and the lover of the waters. || 2 ||
He who has surrendered himself, who has given away all his possessions, who bestows auspiciousness, who is a mass of compassion;
he who is the inspirer of pride, who delights in inspiring pride, and whose form surpasses the height of pride.
The one who causes pride, the one who knows the arts of pride, the one worshipped by the proud;
the one who removes pride, the one who steals the speed of the prideful steed, and the destroyer of pride. || 4 ||

The one who destroys pride, the one worshipped by the eyes of Cupid, the sovereign over Cupid; the one who brings an end to pride, the garlanded with pride, the one who humbles the pride of Cupid. || 5 ||
The destroyer of pride, the giver of pride, the renouncer of pride, the one who has transcended pride, the self-controlled;
the bearer of *darbha* grass, the maker of *darbha*, the subduer, the one established on *darbha*, and the one seated upon a *darbha* mat.
Beloved by the Danavas, praised by the Danavas, the remover of the delusion of the sons of Danu;
the slayer of the Danavas, the conqueror of the Danavas, the destroyer of the prosperity of the Danavas. || 7 ||
The Tamer, the Tamer of the tamable, the Maker of Taming, the one to be venerated by the tamed, the Beloved of the tamed;
the Knower of the yoga beginning with Taming, the one to be tamed, the Play of the tamed, and whose very nature is Taming. || 8 ||
He who seeks self-restraint is attainable through the perfection of self-restraint; he is honored by self-restraint.
He is self-restraint itself, he is to be esteemed for self-restraint, his root is self-restraint, and he is the bestower of what is desired through self-restraint. || 9 ||

He is the self-controlled, whose eyes are controlled, and who has subdued the objects dear to the senses; he is the one who bestows self-restraint, who resembles the subduer of demons, the god of self-control, and the abode of self-restraint.

He is the source of compassion, rooted in compassion, subject to compassion, and devoted to the vow of compassion; he is compassionate, the lord of those worthy of pity, beloved, and dear to his beloved.
He is the source of pitiable freedom from envy, the delighter of the three-eyed Śiva who is himself pitiable,
the doer of what is dear to the pitiable, the one whose very soul is compassion, and the treasure-house of mercy.
Moistened by compassion, having the Aśvattha tree as his beloved, embraced by compassion, a mass of compassion;
the object of compassion, desired by compassion, attained through compassion, and possessing a gaze that looks upon those worthy of pity. || 13 ||
Enveloped by compassion, full of compassion, with compassion established within his heart;
compassionate, gazing with eyes worthy of pity, an ocean of mercy, and the very dawning of compassion. || 14 ||
He who caused the wind to flee in terror, he who caused the sun to flee in terror, he who caused the fire to flee in terror, and he who caused Indra to flee in terror. || 15 ||
He who has caused death to flee in terror, he who has caused the moon to flee in terror,
he who has caused the hosts of spirits to flee in terror, and he who has caused the gods to flee in terror.
He who wields the terrible weapon, he who is free from fear, he whose eyes are formidable, he who is the cause of fear;
he who is far beyond fear, he who has transcended fear, he whose root is fear, and he who is fond of fear. || 17 ||
He who is the destroyer of the demon Dāruka, the subduer of the wicked, the upholder of the earth, and the beloved of the earth;
he who is the protector of those who turn toward the right path, and who is intent on the destruction of the wicked and the bathing [of the virtuous]. || 18 ||
He who is fond of giving, who is praised by the two Aśvins, who is beloved by the skillful, whose deity is the skillful;
whose throat is a gift, whose appearance is a gift, who is the slayer of distress, and who follows after the gift. || 19 ||

He who causes the enemies to flee with a roar of terror; he by whom the Asuras are afflicted with a roar of terror; he whose great mantra is a roar of terror; he who bestows fearlessness through a roar of terror; he who is the destroyer of the cave-dwellers (or the dispeller of fear).
The one who holds with difficulty, who dwells with difficulty, who sleeps with difficulty, and whose seat is difficult;
the one who causes distress, who takes away distress, who has distress within him, and who transcends all distress. || 21 ||
The poor man, the indigent, the treasure-trove for the destitute;
the dweller in caves, the one residing in caves, the one who sports in caves, and the one fond of caves. || 22 ||
He who is easily attained; the God who is easily accessible; whose abode is in the heart that is easily reached;
the remover of fear and suffering; the crusher of the ego-sense; the one who delights in the petals [of the heart-lotus]; and whose interior is like a petal. || 23 ||
The bestower of grace upon the Dalādana, he who is well-worshipped by Dalādana;
his majesty is sung by Dalāda, and he is fond of the waves of Dalāda. || 24 ||
Feeding upon petals, situated within a wheel of four petals, he is the petal-eater;
moving through two- and three-sided lotuses, he is the piercer who divides the ten-sided lotus.
He is the piercer of the twelve-petaled lotus and the divider of the sixteen-cornered lotus;
residing in the two-petaled [lotus], he bestows the attainment of the thousand-petaled lotus. || 26 ||
He who creates the repetition of two syllables, the two-syllabled one, the destroyer of the pride of the boon-granting Ten-faced one;
he who is dear to the forest, who moves in the forest, who sleeps in the forest, and whose abode is the forest. || 27 ||
He who is far-reaching and whose face is distant; he who has made the furthest shore his goal;
he who wears a garland of fire; he who is the fire itself; and he who destroys the defects of fire.
The witness of the divine, the protector of the divine, the delight of the divine, the abode of the divine;
the cause of the ten, transcending the ten, the support of the ten, and the form of the ten. || 29 ||

He possesses the consciousness of the ten and six bonds; he is the shatterer of the ten and six bonds. He bestows the states of existence; he is the knower of the states of existence, the witness of the states of existence, and the remover of the states of existence.

He who possesses ten weapons, who is to be worshipped by the ten great vidyās, who has fifteen eyes, whose self is characterized by the ten marks, and who is defined by the ten and six statements. || 31 ||
He whose rain was signaled by the sounds produced by the multitude of frogs;
Daśapāla, Daśabala, and Daśendriyavihārakṛt. || 32 ||
He is the presiding lord over the group of ten faculties, his vision transcends the ten faculties,
he is attainable through the ten single-fold qualities, and he is the remover of the impurities of the ten faculties.
He is the impeller of the ten faculties and the knower of the ten faculties;
he is the single measure and object of the ten, and the mover of the ten and one qualities. || 34 ||
He is the knower of the ten stages and the direct perception of truth; his very self is characterized by the vision of reality.
He is worshipped at the ten sites of the horse-sacrifice and is the driver of the chariot of the Ten-faced one.
The remover of the pride of the ten-faced one, the destroyer of the city of the ten-faced one;
the annihilator of the lineage of the ten-faced one, and the one worshipped by the younger brother of the ten-faced one. || 36 ||

He gives joy through his vision; he is the person who reveals [the truth]; he is difficult to behold; he is worthy of being seen; he is a partisan of the One Possessing Ten Powers; and he is the destroyer of the ten afflictions.
He is the one who removes the ten afflictions, the one who bestows the ten directions, the one who is skilled in the ten knots;
he is the one who moves through the ten vital breaths, and his vision is the movement within the ten vital breaths.
His body exceeds ten finger-breadths in height; he belongs to the Dasharha clan and enjoys the sixteen [kingdoms];
he is the destroyer of the enemies who bow down before him with their ten fingers joined in salutation.
He who knows the ten divisions of the Brāhmaṇas, he who effects the ten divisions of the Brāhmaṇas;
he who is worthy of worship by the ten Brāhmaṇas, and he who wards off the ten afflictions. || 40 ||
He knows the defects, he bestows the defects, he is the kinsman of the lords of the defects, and he is the remover of enemies;
he gazes solely upon the defects, he strikes down their factions, and he is the pacifier of the suffering caused by the bitten serpent.
Dadhikrā, Dadhikrāvagāmin, Dadhyañc, the bestower of desired boons to sages (Munīṣṭada), Dadhipriya, Dadhisnāta, Dadhipa, and Dadhisindhuga. || 42 ||
O you who are yogurt, whose limbs are smeared with yogurt, and who are adorned with yogurt and unbroken grains;
you who delight in drops of yogurt, whose body is not easily perceived even by those well-versed in the Vedas.
He is the burner, the support of burning, the small one, and the abode of the small; he is the seer of the small, the space within the small, and the ender of the covering of the small. || 44 ||

One whose delusion is burnt away, whose desire is burnt away, whose affliction is burnt away, whose envy is burnt away; one whose sense of duality is burnt away, whose pride is burnt away, whose mental anguish is burnt away, and whose latent tendencies are burnt away. || 45 ||
He who has burnt away misfortune, burnt away hardship, burnt away affliction, and burnt away evil deeds;
he who has burnt the city of the Asuras, burnt the worlds, and burnt away all that is virtuous.
The skillful one, the destroyer of Dakṣa’s sacrifice, the subduer of Dakṣa, the one honored by Dakṣa;
he whose feet are worshipped by those of the south, and who possesses the noble nature of those of the south. || 47 ||
He is the lord of the south, the master of the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), and he whose sacrifice is established by the dakṣiṇā;
he has bestowed the world upon the dakṣiṇā and is devoid of right, left, and so forth. || 48 ||
He who knows the southern and northern paths, who is worthy of gifts and a recipient of offerings;
he who takes refuge in trees, whose dwelling is in trees, who sleeps under trees, and who is fond of trees. || 49 ||
He who bestows birth from trees, who dwells in trees, who destroys the cycle of existence through his tree-like form;
he who is clothed in bark, who is the vessel (Droṇa), who resides in a trough (droṇī), and who is honored by Droṇa. || 50 ||
The wielder of the mallet, the one whose weapon is the mallet, the disciple of the tree, the upholder of the dharma of the tree;
he whose purpose is wealth, the giver of wealth, the driver away [of enemies], and the one dear to the Dravidas. || 51 ||

He who swiftly causes the downfall of prostrating sins, whose fruit is immediate, who knows the path of the swift center [of the heart], who bestows a very long life, and who grants grace most speedily—[to him I bow]. (52)
Quickly satisfied, surpassing swift movement, eating quickly;
subsisting on fruits and leaves, he took delight in bathing in the Dr̥ṣadvatī river.
He who is the one to be worshipped by Drupada, whose intellect is swift, who is skilled in making things rapid,
who possesses swift joy, who maintains speed, and who is expert in the play of rapidity.
Firm, of firm form, steadfastness itself, of firm being, and of firm vows;
firm in his departure, of firm strength, and the one who wards off attachment to firm objects. || 55 ||
He whose intellect is firm, whose vision is firm devotion, who bestows the boon of firm devotion;
he who knows firm vision and firm devotion, who is himself firmly devoted, and who is the firm refuge. || 56 ||
He possesses a firm staff, he is the firm Yama, he is the giver of firmness, and he has made his limbs firm;
he has a firm body, firm meditation, firm practice, and a firm posture. || 57 ||

He who removes the defects of vision, he who is resplendent in the pair of eyes, he who is preceded by sight, he who transcends the mind of sight, he whose movement is purified by sight, and he who is the goal of sight. 58.
He is seen by vision, yet not subject to the range of vision; he is the cause of vision and has vision as his body.
He is attainable through vision, endowed with the three types of vision, and resplendent with an abundance of vision. || 59 ||
Lord of heaven, beholder of heaven, dwelling in heaven, jewel of heaven, initiator of heaven;
embodied as heaven, moving through heaven, stationed in heaven, source of heaven, refuge of heaven, and possessed of heaven.
He removes the defects of day, sleep, movement, light, and dwelling in heaven;
he is the enjoyer of heaven, the performer of gambling, the taker of stakes, the remover of the faults of gambling, and one who stays far from gambling.
The proud one, the destroyer of the proud, dwelling in heaven, the guardian of heaven, the maker of his abode in heaven;
he who has put his enemies to flight, who has driven away minor death, and who has dispelled all deceit.
He who beholds the junction of heaven and earth, who upholds heaven and earth, who perceives the light;
who creates the sky, who illuminates the heart, who is the radiant one; whose eyes are luminous, and who is the kindler of light. || 63 ||
Rooted in light, his own self illuminated, he is the light that is heaven, illuminating all things;
he is the hater of the doctrines of those who maintain duality, and the ender of the doctrines of those who maintain duality.
Victorious over those who propound duality, he cuts down those who propound the two initiations;
he is sixteen years of age, honored by sixteen kings, and possesses twelvefold activity.
The storehouse of the digits of the moon, wearing a tiger skin, the creator of the sixty-four arts;
he who delights in the sixty-four modes of service, whose body consists of the sixty-four musical notes, and who is the destroyer of the two [ignorance and action]. 66.
He is known as the two-syllabled one; he fulfills desired objects through twenty million recitations of his own mantra;
he is the two-footed, the dual-natured, the twice-heavy, the lord of the two worlds, the one who transcends duality, and the illuminator of the two-fold reality. || 67 ||
He whose nature has become dual, who pacifies the duality of consciousness that has become divided, who is the support of the fourteen worlds, and who is the Lord of the fourteen worlds. || 68 ||
Abiding within the fourteen worlds, consisting of the fourteen worlds, the creator of the fourteen worlds, the sovereign of the fourteen worlds, he who has two feet. (69)

He who possesses the fourteenfold knowledge and supernormal powers, who illuminates the fourteenfold knowledge, who is the source of the fourteenfold knowledge, and who bestows the fourteenfold station of Indra. (70)
He is to be honored by fourteen [times] and worshipped by fourteen;
he is the god of fourteen and the creator of half of fourteen manvantaras.
The uprooter of forty-two [afflictions], praised in forty-two kalās; the protector of the two-year-old cow that has two udders and touches the milk; the one who eats twice.
He is the creator of the two-fold creation, the twofold, the one to be praised by the twice-born, the path of the twice-born,
the performer of the duties of the twice-born, the twice-born himself, the one honored by the twice-born, the god of the twice-born, and the creator of the twice-born.
The one most dear to the twice-born, the best among the twice-born, the excellent ornament of the king of the twice-born;
the elder brother of the king of the twice-born, the destroyer of enemies, the destroyer of pride, and the excellent food for the faces of the twice-born.
He has the face of a twice-born, is devoted to the twice-born, sustains the twice-born, and is honored by the twice-born;
he is twofold, possesses two enclosures, wards off dualities, and consumes from two mouths.
He is the protector of the twice-born, the preceptor of the twice-born, and whose throne is the king of birds (Garuḍa).
He is two-footed, the thread for the double-tongued (serpents), the canopy of the hoods of the double-tongued, and the lord of the double-tongued.
He whose self is twelvefold, who perceives the Dvāpara age, who takes the form of the twelve Ādityas;
the lord of the twelfth day, who bears the twelve-spoked wheel, and who consists of twelve syllables. || 77 ||
He who completes the fast on the twelfth day, who transcends the twelfth, who possesses the twelve sixfold powers,
and who is expert in the movement of the seventy-two thousand channels of the body.
The one who causes pairs [of opposites], the one who is beyond pairs, the one who is loathsome to pairs, the one who torments pairs;
the one who removes the suffering of pairs, the one who endures pairs, the one who is free from duality, the one who transcends pairs, and the one who has gone beyond the two.
He who is the door, the one pierced by the door, the one stationed at the door, the upholder of the door, the lover of Dvārakā;
he who creates the door, goes through the door, emerges through the door, and attains liberation through the sequence. || 80 ||
The sustainer of the door, the one who reveals the cycle of existence through the ninefold path of the door;
the son of two mothers, free from duality, and the one who delights in the forest of duality.
Untouched by duality, yet moving within duality, he is expert in the paths of both duality and non-duality;
he is the giver, fond of givers, the forest fire, the terrible one, and the devourer of enemies.
He is the giver, the dwelling place of wood, the knower of servitude, and he who is served by servants;
he is fond of giving, satisfied by giving, the knower of giving, and the embodiment of giving. || 83 ||
He who is fond of servants, the protector of servants, the giver of servants, the one who delights servants;
he whose heart is warm toward his servants, he who is to be served by the self-controlled, the knower of the self-controlled, and the beloved of the self-controlled. || 84 ||
He is the giver, the one whose hair is the act of giving, the one who moves through the forest of giving, and the protector of the forest of giving;
he is the creator of inheritance, the enjoyer of the inheritance, and the one who demonstrates the rules for the acceptance of a wife. || 85 ||
He who is honored by his wife, who is devoid of a wife, who is highly esteemed by his wife;
he who possesses gifts, the enemy of the Dānavas, and the destroyer of the Dānava lineage.

Dāmodara, the maker of bonds, whose consciousness is intent on love for his wife, who is smeared with dārvī-paste, who is deluded by his wife, and who is filled with curiosity for his daughter. || 87 ||
He is the one who rescues the maiden, the giver of the wooden chariot,
the creator of heat, the knower of the pacification of burning, and the presiding deity of Dākṣāyaṇī.

He whose seed-syllable is *drāṃ*, who is perceived as restrained, pacified, and ceased by the mantra *drāṃ*, is the creator of the divine, the knower of the divine, the divine one, he who touches the heavens, and the bestower of the objects desired by the gods. || 89 ||
He is the guardian of the quarters, the lord of the lords of the quarters, and his fame rolls through the cardinal and intermediate directions;
he is the one who reveals the directions, the one whose self is seen, and the one who brings about the vision of the divine.
He is the seen, the giver of examples, the one who transcends examples, and is devoid of examples;
he is destiny, yet free from the limitations of destiny, and the ordainer of destiny.

He whose movement is directed by destiny, who performs both the ordained and the unordained, who impels destiny, who bestows destiny, who destroys destiny, and who pacifies the fruits of ill-fated actions. || 92 ||
He who pervades the world by his destiny, who proclaims the auspiciousness of destiny, and who exerts himself for the sake of destiny;
he who is dear to Diti, praised by Diti, worshipped by Diti, and the bestower of what is desired by Diti. || 93 ||
A forest fire to the heretics, devoted to the daily conduct of the quarters,
he was sky-clad, possessed of divine luster, divine fragrance, and divine food.
He is of divine nature, intensely radiant, the destroyer of faults, and possessed of glowing eyes;
he is long-lived, far-sighted, long-limbed, and long-armed.
He is of far-reaching fame, of far-reaching movement, broad-chested, and long-striding;
he is the one to be served by the wretched, the kinsman of the wretched, the protector of the wretched, and one whose inner being is illuminated. || 96 ||
The uplifter of the distressed, possessing radiant splendor, whose path is the shining sugarcane juice;
sporting, worthy of worship by the initiated, the giver of initiation, the supreme among the initiated. || 97 ||

He performed the initiatory sacrifice (*dīkṣaṇīyeṣṭi*), was expert in the two types of initiation (*dīkṣā*), was fond of initiation, did not eat the food of the initiated, performed initiations, and showed respect for those who were initiated. || 98 ||
The one worthy of initiation, the consumer of the food of the initiated, the fulfiller of the desires of the initiated;
skilled in initiation, whose self is the initiated, and who destroys the pride of the radiant initiated. 99.
He is the great destroyer of evil karma, the knower of what is badly done, the doer of the difficult, and the purifier of evil deeds.
He is the witness of evil acts, the remover of evil deeds, the taker away of evil, and the giver of relief from the suffering caused by evil. || 100 ||
He is the end of evil deeds, the performer of difficult tasks, the warder-off of the density of evil actions;
he is the abandoner of base lineages, the purifier of the wicked, and the destroyer of low-born families. || 101 ||
He is the remover of the sins of low-born families, the guide for those who have gone astray through evil deeds, the performer of difficult tasks,
the destroyer of wicked stains, the one difficult to provoke, and the crusher of thorns that cause suffering.
He performs difficult deeds and undergoes difficult austerities; he is the giver of suffering and the cause of suffering.
He removes the threefold suffering and bestows the threefold suffering; he gives the suffering of suffering. || 103 ||
He who knows the affliction of the threefold suffering, who is honored by those in pain, and who brings suffering to an end;
he who is himself free from suffering, who is devoted to those free from suffering, and who purifies all suffering. || 104 ||
He who creates suffering, who subdues suffering, and who is the enemy of those in pain;
he who removes suffering, who has transcended suffering, who destroys the cause of suffering, and who wards off the affliction of the misery of suffering. || 105 ||

He destroys the defects of evil planetary aspects, he is the destroyer of the misfortunes of suffering, he removes the afflictions of the periods of malefic planets, and he brings about favorability from malignant planets. (106)

He is one who does not take what results in suffering, who indicates the course of existence that results in suffering, who renounces objects that result in suffering, and who perceives the defects in objects that result in suffering. || 107 ||
Durgā, the remover of the suffering of distress, Durgī, the Lord of the Fortress, residing in the Fortress;
the one difficult to reach, whose gait is difficult to follow, the garden of the inaccessible, and the ground of the inaccessible. 108.
He who is to be worshipped by the nine Durgās, he who is praised by the nine Durgās;
the destroyer of fortresses, the one who is difficult to reach, the one who travels on the path that is hard to traverse, and the giver of goals that are difficult to attain.

The destroyer of evil destinies, the giver [of relief] from evil destinies, the one difficult to grasp, the remover of the suffering caused by difficult-to-grasp [influences], the remover of the possession by difficult-to-grasp [influences], and the performer of the subjugation of wicked grahas. || 110 ||
He who dispels the influence of evil planets, the conqueror of malevolent grahas, who is difficult to assail;
he who pacifies the afflictions of false views and removes the fear of wrong perspectives. || 111 ||
He who has transcended all evil qualities, he who is beloved by those who have transcended evil qualities;
the destroyer of foul odors, the one difficult to strike, the one difficult to accomplish, and the one whose actions are difficult to perform. || 112 ||

He is the adversary of evil conduct, the destroyer of diseases difficult to cure, the delighter of those with wicked minds, the teacher of the difficult-to-understand, and the instructor of those who act wrongly. || 113 ||
He is the pacifier of evil thoughts, the turner away from evil intentions and evil desires;
he is difficult to conquer, difficult to digest, difficult to overcome, and the conqueror of the mind that is so hard to know.

He is the remover of that which is difficult to recite, the pacifier of evil rumors, and the destroyer of the defects of a miserable birth; he is the enemy of the wicked, the subduer of the wicked, and the one who causes the wicked to perish.
He is the one afflicted by the wicked, the remover of the suffering of the wicked, the destroyer of the defects of bad water,
the slayer of those who live wickedly, the killer of the corrupt, and the protector of those oppressed by the wicked.
He is the one who puts the wicked to flight, the breaker of evil paths, the remover of association with the corrupt,
the satisfaction that ends a miserable life, and the pinioning of the faces of the base.

He who takes away the enmity of those with difficult lives, the evil eradicator, the one who rescues from the insurmountable, the punisher of the wicked, the shatterer of the corrupt, the slayer of the wicked, and the shaver of the wicked. || 118 ||

He is the pacifier of evil dispositions, the knower of the wicked, and the purifier of the corrupt; he is the heart’s destroyer of evil reasoning, the enemy of false logic, and the bringer of complete relief from the fever of suffering. || 119 ||

He who strikes the drum of ill fortune, he who causes joy by beating the drum, he who removes evil intellect, he who takes away wicked policy, and he who removes the fault of the cry of evil birds. || 120 ||
He is the pacifier of improper practice, the remover of the fault of improper acceptance;
he is the refuge for the weak, the self that is difficult to understand, the cutter of evil bonds, and the one who is hard to transcend. || 121 ||

He is the heart that removes difficult obstacles, the heart that removes terrible fears, whose nature is the pacification of difficult delusions; he is the heart that removes famine, the heart that removes ill-repute, and the pacifier of difficult portents. || 122 ||
He is the one who exposes the flaws in evil counsel, mechanical devices, and tantras; he is the scorcher of wicked friends;
he is difficult to employ, difficult to provoke, difficult to propitiate, and difficult to approach.
He is the savior who crosses the ocean of one's own illusory power, which is difficult to traverse;
he is difficult to restrain, most difficult to attain, and the destroyer of the sin of wicked speech. || 124 ||
He who removes the heart's affliction of an ill name, who purifies those of evil conduct, who is difficult to propitiate;
who takes away the sins of those in wretched hermitages, and whose conscious self-nature is attainable through the path of the difficult.
He who enables one to traverse difficult paths, who purifies those who have eaten forbidden food, and who removes the affliction of sin;
he who takes away the impurity of improper embraces and destroys the evil of illicit sexual union. || 126 ||

He is the ender of chronic diseases, the remover of evil enmity, and the bringer of an end to misfortunes; he is the unconquerable one, the destroyer of ill omens, and the transformer of bad character. || 127 ||
He who removes sorrow and grief, who removes doubt, and who wards off the fear of evil associations;
he whose splendor is unbearable, whose gaze is unbearable, and who destroys the fear of bad dreams. || 128 ||
He purifies the corrupted intellect born from the fault of evil association;
he is the burner of the sins of those who associate with the wicked, and the turner away from the clouds of miserable moments. || 129 ||
He is the purifier of the field of suffering, the remover of the fear of hunger and misery, and the dispeller of the affliction of decay;
he is the destroyer of evil enemies, difficult to know, and the complete cleanser of ignorance.
The messenger, the sole messenger, the lover of messengers, far-reaching, and far-sighted;
the delighter of those with distressed hearts, resembling the dūrvā grass, and the purifier of the corruptible. || 131 ||
The Lord has blazing eyes, a blazing radiance, blazing teeth, a blazing appearance, and a blazing intellect. || 132 ||
Beloved by the gods, the resort of the gods, the goddess, the deity worshipped by the deities;
dear to the Mother of the Gods, the protector of the gods, and the increaser of the gods. || 133 ||
Honored by the gods, worshipped by the gods, speaking kindly to those dear to the world of the gods;
the remover of misfortune for the gods, the bestower of what is desired by the gods, whose very self is the deity.
He is dear to the devotees of the gods, the priest of the gods, honored by the temples of the gods;
he is the thread of the divine lineage, the perfection of the gods, and the excellent instructor of those who harm the gods. || 135 ||
He whose self is the Divine, who is composed of the Divine, who was preceded by the Divine, and who has become the Divine;
he who provides the path to the Divine, who is the teacher of the Divine, and who removes the pride of the Divine. || 136 ||

The destroyer of obstacles on the path of the gods, the upholder of dharma such as sacrifices to the gods, the partisan of the gods, the witness of the gods, and the Sun, the Lord of the gods of gods. || 137 ||
The destroyer of the enemies of the gods, the messenger of the gods, the deity of deities;
the remover of fear from the gods, the one to be sung by the gods, and the consumer of the oblations of the gods. || 138 ||
He who is audible to the gods, visible to the gods, the debt of the gods, and the enjoyer of what is enjoyed by the gods;
the Lord of the Goddesses, the desired object of the Goddesses, the one to be praised by the Goddesses, and the fulfiller of the desires of the Goddesses. || 139 ||
The beloved of the Goddess, the son of Devakī, the guide honored by guides, the one worshipped by guides, the soul of the guides, and the protector of the land of the Goddess’s mother. || 140 ||

The creator of the body, the sustainer of the body, the embodied one, the one who has entered the body, the one who conceives the body, the protector of the body, the giver of the body, and the one who performs his sport within the fourfold body. || 141 ||
He who is to be entreated with the words "Give [me] a body," yet who cuts away the seed of the body;
he who touches the gods and causes the gods to act, yet who does not touch the body and brings about the conception of the body. 142.
Devadatta is the god of gods; though transcending the body, he is the bearer of the body.
He is the temple for the deity that is the body, unattached to the body, and the one who moves at will in the chariot of the body. || 143 ||
He possesses the nature of the body, performs the actions of the body, and is the protector of the body's relations;
he is the giver of the self, the knower of what is to be given and the regions, and he is the creator of space who is himself unconditioned by space.
He is the one who indicates the regions, the possessor of the regions, the native of the regions, the knower of the regions, and the one whose arrival is that of a guide;
he is thoroughly conversant with the languages of the regions, born in the regions, and the purifier of the regions. || 145 ||
Worthy of worship by all lands, he is the one who turns back calamities wrought by the gods;
he is the pacifier of excessive drought, excessive rain, and other such misfortunes ordained by the celestial beings.
He is a reciter of the divine Gāyatrī, a protector of divine prosperity,
one who bestows liberation through the attainment of divine fortune, and one who has reached the state of divinity.
He who removes the demonic nature that clings to the shadow of the lack of divine fortune;
he who bestows grace and grants the fruits of destiny; he who is the Lord of the threefold activity beginning with destiny.

He is the one who approves of destiny, the remover of wretchedness, the deity of astrologers, the knower of destiny, the one worthy of worship by those who know destiny, the divine one, and the cause of misery. 149.

He who removes the paralysis caused by the collyrium of dejection, who bestows the pacification of the three defects, who is the divine physician that removes all faults, and who is endowed with two arms. 150.
He who knows the faults, who fulfills longings, the milker, who is gratified by the one possessing faults;
he who is far from wickedness, who removes wickedness, and who brings peace to the suffering caused by wickedness. || 151 ||
The destroyer of the fault of wickedness, the purifier of wickedness;
the remover of dejection, the performer of missions, and one whose power is manifested through the performance of missions. || 152 ||

He is the remover of misfortune, the destroyer of the sorrow of misfortune, and the pacifier of the pain of misfortune; he is the destroyer of the fault of wickedness, the remover of the defect of low birth, and the subduer of the mental anguish caused by low birth. || 153 ||

He whose equipment consists of venomous serpents, whose weapons are made of venomous serpents, who is clothed in elephant-hide, who has protruding tusks, and who has destroyed the enemies of those with protruding tusks. 154.
The destroyer of the uneven, the wielder of the staff, the illuminator of the science of governance;
the bestower of the purpose of the couple, the one who transcends the state of husband and wife, and the granter of the desires of the couple. || 155 ||
He who pacifies the enmity of husband and wife, he who increases the love of husband and wife;
he whose teeth serve as a mortar, the tusked one, he whose mouth is his tusks, and he who precedes the elephant.
Bearing the thunderbolt, he is the remover of deceit; he punishes those deserving of punishment and wards off the biting insects of affliction.
He is the refuge for those fleeing in haste, and the bestower of elephants, horses, chariots, and infantry.

May he who causes distress to the world wandering in transmigration, who relies upon the three-fold staff, who holds a staff in his hand, who is praised by Vāsudeva, and who is the wielder of the staff, protect us. 158.
Thus ends the glorious *Sahasranāma* beginning with the letter *Da*, which bestows the state of supreme bliss upon those who read or even hear it. (159)

Thus ends the *Dattasahasranāmastotra* beginning with the letter *Da*, composed by the most venerable, supreme *paramahaṃsa* wandering ascetic (*parivrājaka*), the eminent sage Śrī Śrī Śrī Mad Vāsudevānanda Sarasvatī.
